newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish gov't losing grip on economy -S-E-Banken.
newsitem.headline: Swedish gov't losing grip on economy -S-E-Banken.

text.p: The government's economic policy has begun to wobble alarmingly, reducing the chances of further interest rate cuts, S-E-Banken's chief economist Klas Eklund wrote in a circular to clients on Friday.
"Instead of further steps towards stability, we get toing and froing, one step back and then a return to square one," said Eklund, one of the country's most respected economists.
His negative view of government policy and the possible impact on Sweden's international standing was a factor in Swedish bond yields rising on Friday morning, money market traders said.

Listing the government's indecision over a number of issues, first and foremost, whether or not to join the European exchange rate mechanism as a prelude to Economic and Monetary Union, Eklund suggested that years of improvement in state finances - applauded by the markets - were now at risk.
Furthermore, "its policy means Sweden will land on the fringes of the inner circle in Europe. It is difficult to see the advantage in that."
